examples: The lawman rode into town.

The lawman helped the town.

more.def: A person such as a sheriff whose job is to make sure people follow the law, often in the Old West.
examples: The lawman wore a silver star on his coat.
In the old story, the lawman rode into town on a horse.
The town's lawman helped a lost child find her mother.

easy.def: The grass in front of or behind a house.
examples: Dad mows the lawn.
The lawn is green.
I play on the lawn.

more.def: An area of short, cut grass near a house or in a park.
examples: Dad mows the lawn every Saturday.
Children played on the lawn.
The sprinkler watered the front lawn.

easy.def: A case in court.
examples: The company had a lawsuit.
The lawsuit was long.
He filed a lawsuit.

more.def: A case that is brought to a court of law when one person says another has wronged them.
examples: The company faced a lawsuit.
The lawsuit lasted two years.
She filed a lawsuit against the store.

easy.def: A person with a job helping people with the law.
examples: The lawyer works in court.
My aunt is a lawyer.
A lawyer reads many laws.

more.def: A person whose job is to give advice about laws and speak for people in court.
examples: My aunt is a lawyer who helps families.
The lawyer spoke to the judge.
Lawyers study the law for many years.

easy.def: To put something down gently.
examples: Lay the book on the table.
Mom laid the baby in the crib.
Lay your coat here.

more.def: To put something down in a flat or careful way.
examples: Lay the cards face down on the table.
She laid the baby in the crib.
Workers laid bricks in a neat row.

easy.def: To make an egg.
examples: Hens lay eggs.
The hen laid an egg.
Birds lay eggs in nests.

more.def: To produce an egg from the body.
examples: Chickens lay eggs almost every day.
The turtle crawled up the beach to lay her eggs.
Robins lay blue eggs in the spring.

easy.def: A way to pay a little at a time and get the thing later.
examples: Mom put the coat on layaway.
We used layaway for the bike.
The toy is on layaway.

more.def: A plan in which a store keeps an item for you while you pay for it in small amounts over time.
examples: Dad put the winter coat on layaway and paid a little each week.
The store lets shoppers use layaway for big gifts.
She bought the bicycle on layaway and picked it up in the spring.

easy.def: One flat piece over another.
examples: The cake has three layers.
A layer of snow.
Put on a layer of paint.

more.def: A flat thickness of something that covers a surface or lies between other things.
examples: The cake had three layers.
A layer of snow covered the road.
I wore a sweater as a second layer.

easy.def: A person who is not an expert.
examples: He is a layman.
A layman can learn it.
The layman asked questions.

more.def: A person who is not trained in a certain subject or job.
examples: The doctor explained the illness in words a layman could understand.
A layman may not know the science words.
The book is written for the layman.

easy.def: The way things are set out on a page or in a place.
examples: I like the layout of the page.
The layout of the room is nice.
We changed the layout.

more.def: The way that parts of something are arranged on a page, a map or in a room.
examples: The layout of the room made it easy to move around.
I drew the layout of my dream bedroom.
The book has a clear layout, with pictures next to the words.

easy.def: Not wanting to work or move.
examples: The lazy cat slept all day.
I feel lazy on hot days.
A lazy dog lay in the sun.

more.def: Not willing to work or use energy.
examples: He felt too lazy to get up and close the door.
We spent a lazy afternoon reading by the pool.
He was too lazy to put his dishes in the sink.
